# Release notes
## Mac and connected devices
- **All your Macs in one sidebar:** When your Controller account has more than one Mac, the Mac now opens in **All Environments**, as the iPhone can: every Mac's chats appear in one sidebar, each row naming its Mac, and choosing a chat opens it on the Mac it lives on. Pick **This Mac** or a single Mac from the environment menu at the bottom of the sidebar to go back to one; Controller remembers your choice. - **Start a project on whichever Mac:** With every Mac showing, **New Thread** lists the projects on all of them and searches their names too. Copies of the same Git repository on different Macs sit together and say which other Macs have it, so you can start the same project on either one. An empty chat's headline names its Mac; choose the project on another Mac and the draft moves there with its text. - **Agents across your Macs:** Agents can now see your other Macs with `list_projects` and `orchestration_capabilities`, and start, read, message, wait on, stop and close threads on another Mac by naming it. They reach only that Mac's copy of the same repository and never get more access than they have themselves. Reports when a thread on another Mac finishes come in a later update; for now agents check on it themselves. - **iPhone opens on all your Macs:** With more than one Mac in your account, the iPhone opens in **All Environments** until you pick a single Mac. New Chat also says which other Macs have a copy of each project. - **Usage adds up every Mac:** The Usage window now combines an account used on several Macs into one line, such as one Claude Code row instead of one per Mac, and its title stays **Usage** when it covers all of them. The **Devices** card still shows each Mac's share. - **Antigravity reasoning:** Antigravity's models now offer a reasoning-effort choice instead of separate high and low copies of each model, and its tool calls show richer details. Thinking from Antigravity and other agents connected over ACP streams into the conversation like other agents' reasoning, with summaries where the agent sends them. - **Clearer OpenCode and Claude Code activity:** OpenCode accepts reasoning variants by their usual names, and Claude Code commands are classified as reads, searches and edits as they run.

## Mac and connected devices
- **Chats without a project:** Start a thread with **No Project** from the New Thread palette, **File → New Thread Without a Project** (Option-Command-N), or **Start Without a Project** in an empty window. Each one works in a new folder of its own under `~/Controller`, named after its first message, so whatever the agent makes is easy to find. Deleting the thread keeps its folder. On iPhone, **New Chat** lists **No Project** for each Mac that offers it. - **Factory Droid threads stay separate:** Two Droid threads in the same project no longer show each other's conversation. Each thread now runs in its own Droid process, so starting a second one no longer ends the first one's turn. - **No more "Plan is up-to-date.":** Droid's internal reply to its own to-do reminder no longer appears as the end of a turn, on the Mac, on iPhone or in thread previews. Transcripts saved before this update still show it. - **Clearer Claude Code history:** Commands Claude Code ran in saved transcripts now show as the reads, searches and edits they were, the same way Codex commands do, with the full command still available.

- **Google Antigravity:** Add an Antigravity account in Settings → Providers. Controller downloads Google's Antigravity agent, checks that Google signed it, and shares it between all your Antigravity accounts. **Sign in with Google** opens Google's page in your browser; each account keeps its sign-in in its own private profile, and Controller never sees your tokens. Gemini Enterprise, Gemini API keys and Agent Platform (Vertex AI) also work. Approval modes, the agent's questions and its tool output all appear as they do for the other agents. - **Models before the first chat:** Antigravity and Factory Droid now list their models as soon as the account connects, instead of only after the first chat started. Any account that you sign in to after connecting also loads its models straight away. - **Your whole usage history:** The Usage window now includes the history Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Grok and Factory Droid keep on your Mac, including work you did in them directly and work from before Controller was tracking. A conversation Controller also tracked counts once. The first read takes a few seconds; after that only new work is read. - **Usage from all your Macs:** Each Mac shares its usage with your other Macs over Connect, and also through your private iCloud database, so every Mac's Usage window shows everything. A **Devices** card breaks it down once another Mac contributes. Turn off **Sync usage** in Connect settings to keep iCloud out of it. - **Dictation cleanup stays in place:** While Apple Intelligence tidies a dictated message, the corrected text now wraps exactly where the message box does instead of jumping at the end, and on iPhone the microphone, spinner and waveform stay put.
